headline: Researchers at George Washington University have published a formula that estimates how far a chatbot conversation can run before the AI slips into bad answers.
score_reason: Fresh and useful safety research, but tested only on seven small open models and not shown on the big commercial chatbots.
importance_line: Anyone using chatbots or AI agents could eventually get an early warning before an AI starts giving bad output, but so far this is a team's own result on open models, with no outside review reported.
summary: SecurityWeek reports that researchers Neil Johnson and Frank Huo of George Washington University derived a formula for the tipping point at which a conversation's accumulated context pushes a chatbot's attention mechanism, the part that decides which earlier text matters most, toward bad output, and tested it on seven open-weight models of 124 million to 12 billion parameters. Johnson says a simple warning light inside the model could flag the tipping, but the team could add it only to open models, not to the closed systems of OpenAI or Anthropic.
notes: Read in full. Tested on open models only; the paper's review status is not stated.
